hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $\frac{x^2}{x}$: quotient rule gives $\frac{2x \cdot x - x^2 \cdot 1}{x^2} = \frac{x^2}{x^2} = 1$, which is right since $\frac{x^2}{x} = x$. Same recipe with $e^x$ on top.

explanation: At $x = 1$ the factor $(x - 1)$ is $0$, so $h'(1) = 0$. In fact $x = 1$ is where $\frac{e^x}{x}$ bottoms out, at height $e$.

alternativeExplanations.title: See the minimum
steps: The value dips at $x = 1$ and rises on both sides: a valley.
At the bottom of a valley the tangent is flat, so $h'(1) = 0$ is exactly what the picture predicts.
